name: Validators

subjectOf.text: Validator-verified citation correction is insufficient as a standalone remedy because validators may identify obviously missing citations or inflated self-citation yet lack the domain-specific knowledge to assess fine-grained attribution weights.
subjectOf.abstract: A validator may be able to identify obviously missing citations or obviously inflated self-citation, but may lack the domain-specific knowledge to assess fine-grained attribution weights.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Citation Honesty Mechanisms in Weighted Directed Acyclic Graph Governance (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6269518
scope_conditions: validators lack complete knowledge of the relevant citation history

subjectOf.text: Under a decoupled payment formula in which validators rank quality and citation accuracy as separate dimensions, an agent who produces medium-quality work but cites meticulously can still earn substantial payment through the citation honesty component.
subjectOf.abstract: Validators rank both quality and citation accuracy as separate dimensions. An agent who produces medium-quality work but cites meticulously can still earn substantial payment through the ηi component.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Citation Honesty Mechanisms in Weighted Directed Acyclic Graph Governance (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6269518
scope_conditions: validators rank quality and citation accuracy separately
payment weight parameter theta strictly below one

subjectOf.text: Awarding validators a reputation bonus for detecting under-citation that consensus agrees with creates a positive incentive for vigilant citation policing.
subjectOf.abstract: Validators receive a reputation bonus for detecting under-citation that consensus agrees with, creating a positive incentive for vigilant citation policing.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Citation Honesty Mechanisms in Weighted Directed Acyclic Graph Governance (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6269518
scope_conditions: consensus agreement on the detected under-citation

subjectOf.text: The citation honesty equilibrium is robust because it does not require agents to quantify precise citation weights; it requires only that citation patterns be directionally honest, which is what the validator assessment evaluates, thereby addressing the quantification impossibility.
subjectOf.abstract: It requires only that agents' citation patterns be directionally honest. That is, citation patterns demonstrate that agents do not systematically under-cite contributors whose work they relied upon.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Citation Honesty Mechanisms in Weighted Directed Acyclic Graph Governance (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6269518
scope_conditions: validators assess directional honesty rather than point estimates of attribution fractions

subjectOf.text: The channel the RLRF program claims reputation can resist is the one this study does not open, because its validators are stationary, its stake has no external value, and its weights are fixed before generation 1.
subjectOf.abstract: Intelligence models increasingly learn from data that earlier Intelligence models produced, and when that loop repeats the rare cases disappear first. This paper preregisters a test of whether a reputation-weighted validator pool, filtering the training data of a recursive replacement loop, keeps those rare cases alive. The outcomes remain sealed until a replication of the original model-collapse result succeeds.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Can Reputation Prevent Model Collapse? A Preregistered Test of Reputation-Weighted Data Filtering (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7598518
scope_conditions: The limit is structural, set by the design, rather than an observed null.
Goodhart resistance is the property the parent program claims, so this study leaves that claim untested.
